newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans say conditions for women improved - survey.
newsitem.headline: Germans say conditions for women improved - survey.

text.p: More than two-thirds of Germans believe the situation for women has improved in the decades following the feminist movement which began in the 1970s, a television poll showed on Friday.
In a survey published ahead of International Women's Day on March 8, Deutsche Welle television found 68 percent of Germans surveyed agreed conditions for women had improved in the last two decades.
Only 12 percent said they felt conditions for women had worsened since the 1970s, while 14 percent said nothing had changed, Deutsche Welle said in a statement.
The poll was conducted this week by the Forsa research institute and surveyed more than 1,000 men and women.
"There was a considerable difference in the view of the situation between east and west Germans," the network said.

While about 75 percent of west Germans agreed women's conditions had improved, only 35 percent of east Germans thought that was the case. The survey found 44 percent of easterners believed the situation had worsened compared to only four percent of westerners.
